adjudication_label: influence of simulation boundary conditions on stacking fault morphology
canonical_question: Is the 'parallel distribution' of stacking faults in the <1-12> orientation a result of the specific crystallographic orientation or the simulation boundary conditions?

question_variants.question: Is the 'parallel distribution' of stacking faults in the <1-12> orientation a result of the specific crystallographic orientation or the simulation boundary conditions?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text attributes the parallel distribution of stacking faults to the activation of only one slip system, which is determined by the crystallographic orientation, rather than boundary conditions.

answers.answer: The text states: 'However, the stacking faults induced by the motion of Shockley partial dislocations displayed a parallel distribution, indicating that only one slip system was activated during dislocation slip. The applied strain did not trigger other slip systems.' This implies the orientation dictates the single active system, rather than boundary conditions.
evidence_spans: The primary dislocations observed were Shockley partial dislocations and stair-rod immobile dislocations.
No BCC atoms were observed in any of the three orientations, indicating that no FCC-to-BCC phase transformation occurred during tensile deformation.
The yield strength of the alloy was relatively insensitive to strain rate within the simulated range.
